findings.message: Preserve unfilled circles for point legends. The absence of a fill color does not imply a line geometry. `DEFAULT_USER_LAYER_LEGEND` in `src/features/create_layer/constants.ts` explicitly labels its circle step “Point” and supplies only `color` and `width`, so this change renders that point legend as a horizontal line. Preserve hollow circles for circle steps and use an explicit shape or geometry discriminator for line legends.

With this change, every `circle` legend step that has no fill now renders as a horizontal line. That includes point layers. `DEFAULT_USER_LAYER_LEGEND` (src/features/create_layer/constants.ts:37-46, a 'Point' step with only `color`/`width`) and `registerNewGeometryLayer` (src/core/logical_layers/utils/registerNewGeometryLayer.ts:33-39, only `color`) both reach this branch, as do backend legends that style point markers with only `circle-stroke-color`. Users would see a line symbol for point features, which is misleading. Make the line an explicit opt-in instead of switching on missing fill, e.g. a new `line` step shape or a flag.

This deep-imports an internal build path (`@konturio/default-icons/tslib/figma-icons/Letter.js`). The rest of the codebase, including MultivariateLegend.tsx:2, uses the public `import { Letter } from '@konturio/default-icons'`. Internal paths can move or be blocked by package `exports` in any version bump, which breaks the build or the vitest mock resolution. Import from the package root instead.

When `text-color` is missing, the letter icon is forced to `#000000`, but the label gets no color and inherits the theme color. That contradicts the stated goal that the icon matches the label, and it shows as black-on-dark in dark contexts. Omit the color, or use `currentColor`/inherit, when `text-color` is absent.

The test asserts the exact SVG path data (`M6 6H18V9.08508...`) from the third-party icon package. Any harmless icon redesign in a dependabot bump will fail this test. Assert on something stable instead, e.g. mock the icon or check that an svg is rendered with the expected color.

Only the no-fill branch is tested. No test checks that a circle (with the correct fill/stroke) still renders when `fill` or `circle-color` is provided, so a regression in the main path would go unnoticed.

The line branch triggers only on the exact sentinel string 'none'. Callers or styles that pass `fill-color: 'transparent'` or an rgba with zero alpha still get an outline circle, so outline circles are not fully replaced as the PR intends. The behavior is inconsistent.

CircleIcon now draws a horizontal line whenever no fill is set, and this applies to every circle legend step. Existing point legends have no fill: `DEFAULT_USER_LAYER_LEGEND` (src/features/create_layer/constants.ts:37-46, step name 'Point', only `color`/`width`) and the drawn-geometry layer legend in registerNewGeometryLayer.ts:33-39 (only `color`). Both will now show a line next to a 'Point' label, which tells users the wrong geometry type. Make the line an explicit opt-in (for example a new 'line' stepShape, or a flag on the step) instead of changing what 'circle' means everywhere.

The line-or-circle decision is a plain string check `fillColor === 'none'`. Transparent fills such as 'transparent' or 'rgba(0,0,0,0)' still draw an outline circle, while `fill="none"` passed in from a caller is also treated as 'no fill'. The two cases behave differently even though both mean no visible fill.

The rest of the codebase uses named imports from the package root (`import { X } from '@konturio/default-icons'`). This line deep-imports the package's internal build path (`tslib/figma-icons/Letter.js`). That path isn't part of the public API, so a dependabot version bump can break it without warning. Exhaustive or bundler `exports` maps may also reject it. Import the icon from the package root if it's exported there.

The letter icon gets its color only from CSS `color` on the svg. That works only if the Figma Letter icon uses `currentColor` for its fill or stroke. If its paths hardcode a fill, the icon stays its default color and the stated goal (icon matches label color) fails. The test can't catch this because it only checks the svg's `style` attribute, not the color actually applied to the path. Check the icon's markup, or test the path's fill/stroke against `currentColor`.

When `text-color` is missing, the icon falls back to a hardcoded '#000000', while the label (lines 51-54) inherits the theme text color. On dark themes or with non-black default text, the icon and label won't match, which contradicts the 'matches the label' goal. Leave `color` unset or use 'currentColor' so both inherit the same color. Also, `stepIconFill`/`stepIconStroke` are silently ignored for letter steps.

The test depends on implementation details: an exact SVG path prefix from a third-party icon, which any icon package update can change, and the raw `style` attribute string. If the DOM normalizes colors to rgb() it fails, and it passes even when the color doesn't actually reach the drawn path. Also, nothing tests the fallback when `text-color` is absent, and the existing circle-with-fill path isn't covered.

Only the no-fill case is tested. Nothing checks that a filled circle still renders a `<circle>` with the right fill and stroke, or that the line gets the expected stroke color and width. A regression in the default (filled) branch would go unnoticed.
